summary: A JUnit test class that checks a Thermostat object reports the right status — "Heating", "Idle", or "Cooling" — at several temperatures, in both normal mode and energy-saving eco mode.

lines.text: Brings in the @Test annotation from JUnit 5, which is what marks a method as a test the runner should execute.
A static import so you can write assertEquals(...) directly instead of Assertions.assertEquals(...), keeping each test line short and readable.
By convention the test class is named after the class under test with Test appended, so tools and readers can pair them at a glance.
The method name states the expected behaviour in full, so a failure report tells you what broke without your having to read the body.
Builds a thermostat at 60 degrees with eco mode off; a fresh object per test means no test can be affected by another one.
Compares the expected value against the actual one, and the expected value always comes first in assertEquals.
72 sits comfortably inside the normal comfort band, so the thermostat should do nothing at all.
76 is just past the normal cooling threshold, a boundary value chosen deliberately because bugs cluster at edges.
Passing true turns on eco mode, which tolerates cooler rooms before heating; 64 is cold enough to trigger heating even so.
66 would call for heating in normal mode but counts as idle in eco mode, which is exactly the difference this test pins down.
Eco mode lets the room get warmer before cooling, so it takes 79 rather than 76 to trigger cooling.
Tests the display text separately from the status logic, so a change in wording fails one focused test rather than several.
